text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: service=prefill-us-west-2 severity=high — sudden spike in GPU OOMs during prefill. ~6 container restarts in last 2m. Affected model: gpt-large-v1-q4. Pager: @alice_oncall. Link: https://redwood.inc/incident/1767543210

alice_oncall: On it. Ping @bob_runtime @carol_sre. Starting live mitigation coordination.

bob_runtime: Looking now. Quick triage: CUDA OOMs reported on node gpu-w-12 during long prefill requests. Suspect very large context windows. Attaching recent logs.

bob_runtime: ```[2026-03-17T21:20:11Z] runtime ERROR cuda out of memory: 0 bytes free on device 0
[2026-03-17T21:20:12Z] prefill: request_id=abc123 context_tokens=95000 seq_len=120000
[2026-03-17T21:20:13Z] container restart triggered: SIGKILL```

carol_sre: Confirmed node shows high GPU mem fragmentation plus a node-flap at 21:05. I'll cordon gpu-w-12 and move prefill pods off it. Scheduling deeper hardware diag after incident.

alice_oncall: Mitigation proposal: 1) Temporary throttle for prefix length >= 60k tokens on prefill route. 2) Route very large requests to cpu-coldmodel fallback. Who can flip routing?

frank_prod: I can push a routing rule via Console. Creating a canary: if context_tokens > 60000 -> fallback_model_cold, canary 10% then 100%. Kicking it off now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: update=prefix-throttle-rule by frank_prod (canary 10%) — https://console.redwood/rollouts/1767543210

dave_support: We're seeing a handful of 500s from customers. Ticket INC-1124 from AcmeCorp with examples. CS looped in @eve_cs.

eve_cs: Messaged AcmeCorp, gave a 15m ETA and noted we're applying mitigations. Getting example request_ids. They reported duplicate retries causing extra load.

bob_runtime: While canary runs, push a small hotpatch to reduce prefill batch_size (32->8) for gpt-large-v1-q4 to reduce peak allocations. Command:```kubectl -n inference set env deploy/prefill RUNTIME_BATCH_SIZE=8 --record``` Applying now.

carol_sre: gpu-w-12 cordoned and pods evicted. Observing other nodes; no restarts on them in last 30s.

alice_oncall: Any kernel/driver resets?

bob_runtime: Found this sequence in dmesg: "NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus" then "cuda: driver lost context" — suggests hardware/driver instability amplified by large allocations.

carol_sre: We'll take gpu-w-12 OOS for replacement after stabilization. Marking for post-incident hardware check.

frank_prod: Canary passed at 10%, promoting throttle to 100%.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: prefix-throttle-rule (100%) — no errors.

dave_support: AcmeCorp reports errors dropped ~4m after mitigations, thanks for the update.

bob_runtime: Observed overall GPU memory usage drop ~40% after batch_size change + throttle. No new OOMs for 8m.

eve_cs: One other customer reported intermittent failures but frequency reduced. Sending consolidated customer update now.

carol_sre: Taking gpu-w-12 out of rotation for hardware replacement and extended diagnostics. Will only reintroduce after validation.

alice_oncall: Primary mitigations effective. Keeping incident open for 2h for data collection and postmortem prep. Follow-ups: eng-runtime to write postmortem, eng-sre to replace node and check driver/kernel, CS to send customer summary. POC: alice_oncall.

frank_prod: Noted. Throttle rule and changes are in audit logs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring) — root cause: large-context prefill allocations + GPU memory fragmentation/hardware instability on gpu-w-12. Immediate actions taken: throttle >60k tokens, reduce runtime batch_size, cordon node gpu-w-12. Follow-ups: eng-runtime postmortem, hardware replacement, and customer communication. Incident owner: alice_oncall.
